terms.meaning: A counting number multiplied by itself: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25…
The number you square to get it. √49 = 7, because 7² = 49. (−7)² is also 49, but here we use only the positive root.
The dots in a triangle: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15… Each one adds the next counting number.
A counting number multiplied by itself three times: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125…
The number you cube to get it. ∛8 = 2, because 2³ = 8.
A number that is the sum of two cubes in two different ways. 1729, the Hardy–Ramanujan number, is the smallest.

items.name: Number of factors
items.formula: Only squares have an odd number of factors

items.name: Last digit of a square
items.example: 2187 ends in 7, so it is not a square.

items.name: Zeros at the end of a square
items.formula: Always an even number of zeros

items.name: Sum of the first n odd numbers
From one square to the next
Two neighbouring triangular numbers
items.formula: Add up to a perfect square

items.name: Square root by prime factors
items.formula: Split the prime factors into two equal groups

items.name: Smallest number to multiply by to get a square
items.formula: Multiply by the prime factors left without a pair

items.name: Finding a square root by narrowing down
items.formula: Use the squares on each side, then the last digit
items.example: √2116 is between 40 and 50, and ends in 4 or 6. 45² = 2025 is too small, so √2116 = 46.

items.name: Nearest whole number for a root
items.formula: Find the two squares it lies between
items.example: 14² = 196 and 15² = 225. 200 is nearer to 196, so √200 is about 14.

items.name: Last digit of a cube
items.formula: 2 ↔ 8 and 3 ↔ 7 swap. Other digits stay the same.
items.example: 18³ = 5832: 18 ends in 8, so its cube ends in 2.

items.name: The Hardy–Ramanujan number
items.example: The next two taxicab numbers are 4104 and 13832.

items.name: Cube root by prime factors
items.formula: Split the prime factors into three equal groups

items.name: Successive differences
items.formula: Squares: all the same after 2 levels. Cubes: after 3 levels.

mistakes.text: A last digit of 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9 does not prove a number is a square. 46 ends in 6 and is not a square. The last digit can only rule a number out.
A number ending in an odd number of zeros cannot be a square. 4000 has three zeros, so it is not a square.
The count 2n leaves out the two squares at the ends. Between 16 and 25 there are 8 numbers, not 10.
A square loses the minus sign, but a cube keeps it. (−6)² = 36, but (−6)³ = −216.
A cube needs three equal groups, not two. 108 = 2² × 3³ has only two 2s, so it is not a cube.
